text.p: SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Parliament will begin its next session on February 4. The preliminary agenda includes amendments to penal code returned by President Michal Kovac for revision, law on creation of Export-Import bank and law on protection against dumping imports.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovak engineering production increased by 15.8 percent year-on-year for the January-October period last year, totalling 69.4 billion cowns.
- The Slovak subsidiary of Germany's Siemens has won a contract to build and operate the public lighting system in Bratislava, worth some two billion crowns.

- Wood processing company Bukoza Vranov said its production totalled 1.36 billion crowns in 1996, with exports accounting for 68 percent. The company plans a modernisation project worth 250 million crowns this year.

NARODNA OBRODA - Four members of the so-called Helsinki committee of the U.S. congress have signed a letter to the parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic asking him to return the mandate to former coalition deputy Frantisek Gaulider. Gaulider was expelled from parliament after he quit the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) last autumn.

PRAVDA - Stefan Gavornik, President of the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, opposes the government's plan to privatise three largest banks by large Slovak companies which are, in most cases, the banks' largest debtors.
